questions.q: State what is meant by a protocol.

markPoints.concept: a set of rules for how devices communicate
markPoints.exemplar: A set of rules for how devices communicate.

questions.example: A set of rules that says how data is to be sent between devices.
questions.paraphrase: Agreed rules governing how machines exchange data.
questions.feedback: Rules for communicating. Without the second half it could be a definition of anything.

questions.q: Explain why standards are needed in computing.

markPoints.concept: they let equipment from different manufacturers work together
markPoints.exemplar: They let equipment made by different companies work together.

markPoints.concept: so a user is not tied to one manufacturer and more devices can be connected
accept: not tied|not locked|locked to one|choice|any device|wider|more devices|free to choose|mix|combine|several suppliers|any manufacturer|cheaper|competition
markPoints.exemplar: So a buyer is not tied to one manufacturer's equipment.

questions.example: Standards mean equipment made by different manufacturers follows the same rules, so it can be connected together — which means a buyer is not tied to one company's products and can mix equipment freely.
questions.paraphrase: Because every maker follows the same agreed rules their devices are compatible, so a customer can combine hardware from several suppliers instead of being locked to one.
questions.feedback: Different manufacturers working together, then why that matters to somebody.

questions.q: Match each protocol to what it is used for.
pairs: Reading email that stays on the server
Splitting data into packets and checking they all arrive
Routing packets across networks to the right address
questions.feedback: SMTP sends, IMAP reads. TCP looks after the packets; IP looks after where they go.

questions.q: A user downloads email so that it is removed from the server and kept on one device. Which protocol is being used?
questions.feedback: POP takes the mail off the server; IMAP leaves it there so several devices can see the same mailbox.

questions.q: Explain the difference between IMAP and POP.

markPoints.concept: POP downloads the email and removes it from the server
markPoints.exemplar: POP downloads the email and removes it from the server.

markPoints.concept: IMAP leaves the email on the server so it can be read from several devices
accept: leaves|stays|remains|kept|stored on the server|several devices|multiple devices|any device|synchronise|sync
markPoints.exemplar: IMAP leaves the email on the server so several devices can see it.

questions.example: POP downloads messages to one device and removes them from the server, so they can only be read there. IMAP leaves them on the server, so the same mailbox can be read from a phone, a laptop and a desktop and stays in step.
questions.paraphrase: With POP the mail is pulled down to a single machine and taken off the server; with IMAP it stays on the server and every device sees the same thing.
questions.feedback: Both halves. The practical difference is whether a second device can see the same mail.
